statement: The function returns Ok r, where r is an m x n integer matrix satisfying: (a) r[i][j] >= 1 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n; (b) for every row i and columns a,b, matrix[i][a] < matrix[i][b] iff r[i][a] < r[i][b], and matrix[i][a] = matrix[i][b] iff r[i][a] = r[i][b]; (c) for every column j and rows a,b, matrix[a][j] < matrix[b][j] iff r[a][j] < r[b][j], and matrix[a][j] = matrix[b][j] iff r[a][j] = r[b][j]; (d) r is pointwise least among all m x n integer matrices S that satisfy (a), (b), and (c) with r replaced by S, meaning r[i][j] <= S[i][j] for all i,j. This is the complete rank-transform specification.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. The rank-transform answer for matrix is unique, as promised by the problem.

statement: The function returns a result for every valid input: there exists r such that matrix_rank_transform(matrix) = Ok r. It does not fail by overflow, out-of-bounds access, or panic.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and -10^9 <= matrix[i][j] <= 10^9 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, the result has the same dimensions as the input: len(r) = m, and len(r[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < m.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, every entry of r is at least 1: for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, r[i][j] >= 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Let D be the number of distinct values appearing among all entries of matrix. Whenever the function returns Ok r, every entry of r is at most D: for all i,j, r[i][j] <= D.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, each row of r preserves the strict order and equality of the corresponding row of matrix: for every row i and every pair of columns a,b, matrix[i][a] < matrix[i][b] iff r[i][a] < r[i][b], and matrix[i][a] = matrix[i][b] iff r[i][a] = r[i][b].
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, each column of r preserves the strict order and equality of the corresponding column of matrix: for every column j and every pair of rows a,b, matrix[a][j] < matrix[b][j] iff r[a][j] < r[b][j], and matrix[a][j] = matrix[b][j] iff r[a][j] = r[b][j].
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, r is pointwise minimal among all m x n integer matrices S that have entries at least 1 and preserve the row and column order/equality relations of matrix. That is, for every such S and every i,j, r[i][j] <= S[i][j].
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, if two cells are connected by a finite chain of equal matrix values where consecutive cells share a row or a column, then those two cells have equal ranks. Formally, if there are t >= 0 and cells (i_0,j_0),...,(i_t,j_t) with (i_0,j_0)=(i,j), (i_t,j_t)=(k,l), and for every 0 <= s < t, matrix[i_s][j_s] = matrix[i_{s+1}][j_{s+1}] and (i_s = i_{s+1} or j_s = j_{s+1}), then r[i][j] = r[k][l].
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Let vmin be the minimum value among all entries of matrix. Whenever the function returns Ok r, every cell containing vmin has rank 1: for all i,j, if matrix[i][j] = vmin then r[i][j] = 1. In particular, at least one entry of r equals 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, let K be the maximum entry of r. Then every integer from 1 through K occurs as a rank: for every integer k with 1 <= k <= K, there exist i,j such that r[i][j] = k.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row of matrix has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r for matrix and Ok r' for matrix', we have r = r' (the two results have identical dimensions and entries).
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row has length n, and entries are within the stated value range. Let c be an integer such that matrix'[i][j] = matrix[i][j] + c is also within -10^9 .. 10^9 for every i,j.

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r for matrix and Ok rT for MT, the transpose relation holds: for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, rT[j][i] = r[i][j].
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row has length n, and entries are within the stated value range. Let MT be the n x m transpose defined by MT[j][i] = matrix[i][j].

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r for matrix and Ok r' for matrix', we have r'[i][j] = r[p(i)][q(j)] for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row has length n, and entries are within the stated value range. Let p be a permutation of {0,...,m-1}, q a permutation of {0,...,n-1}, and define matrix' [i][j] = matrix[p(i)][q(j)].

statement: Whenever the function returns Ok r, for every cell (i,j), let C(i,j) be the set of cells (a,b) reachable from (i,j) by a finite chain in which consecutive cells have equal matrix values and share a row or a column. Then r[i][j] is the largest integer L >= 1 for which there exist cells c_0,...,c_{L-1} such that c_{L-1} is in C(i,j) and, for every 0 <= s < L-1, c_s and c_{s+1} share a row or a column and matrix[c_s] < matrix[c_{s+1}], where matrix[c] denotes the entry of matrix at cell c.
preconditions: Let m = len(matrix) and n = len(matrix[0]). The input is valid: 1 <= m,n <= 500, every row has length n, and entries are within the stated value range.
